methods.label: Chain rule
methods.explanation: The chain rule requires multiplying the derivative of the square by the derivative \(3\) of the inner function \(3x-1\). Thus \(y'=2(3x-1)\times3\). At \(x=1\), this gives \(y'(1)=2\times2\times3=12\).
methods.levelReason: Uses only the simple affine chain rule, the power rule, and substitution.

methods.label: Expand before differentiating
methods.explanation: Expanding the square turns the expression into a polynomial: \(y=9x^2-6x+1\). Differentiating term by term gives \(y'=18x-6\). Therefore \(y'(1)=18-6=12\).
methods.levelReason: Uses perfect-square expansion and polynomial differentiation, requiring no chain rule.
